   [{"slot_number": "slot-10-2-1", "slot_key": "Acceptance criteria for complaint registration and investigation support", "slot_value": "Provide faster complaint registration, easier case status tracking, reliable record retrieval with fewer manual steps, fewer investigation delays, improved coordination between police units, and quicker detection of repeat criminal patterns", "state": "filled", "deferred": false, "is_necessary": true}, {"slot_number": "slot-10-2-2", "slot_key": "Open policy or process decisions", "slot_value": "The system should capture incident location as precisely as possible, along with the date and time of occurrence or discovery; if the exact time or place is unknown, it should still allow an approximate value or best-known description instead of blocking the complaint, and clearly mark those fields as estimated or incomplete so officers know follow-up is needed", "state": "filled", "deferred": false, "is_necessary": false}, {"slot_number": "slot-10-2-3", "slot_key": "Delivery risks and dependency constraints", "slot_value": "Sensitive or high-volume specialized units should be kept out of the first phase until the core complaint and case workflow is stable; the first phase should focus on standard police stations and a few controlled pilot units rather than every specialized team at once; high-volume units like cybercrime, narcotics, or large district control rooms may need to wait unless they can be supported with simpler workflows and enough training, because they tend to generate more exceptions and heavier data loads; units with strong internal discipline and clear case-handling procedures could participate earlier, while units with unusual operating conditions or sensitive data should be brought in more cautiously. parsed_response.slot_key: Dependency outage and approval closure handling
parsed_response.slot_value: If a dependent system is unavailable or the approving office is closed, the request should stay pending with a clear reason and timestamp rather than being dropped; urgent matters should use a fallback manual process so the officer can continue and complete the formal step later, while non-urgent items can wait in a queue and be routed automatically once service resumes. Pending items should remain visible in a suspended or pending state so staff can see they are not lost, with the reason for the delay recorded. If the dependency is unavailable only briefly, items can wait in queue; if the outage exceeds an operational threshold, a manual workaround is allowed only for urgent cases and with supervisor awareness. Once the other system or office is back, the items should resume from where they stopped, and the system should track what was completed manually so nothing gets duplicated. Exceptional overrides after transfer, court send, or closure are allowed only for clerical error, new evidence, court return, or supervisory review showing the case was closed too early; ordinary users cannot do this, approval must come from a supervisor or higher-ranking officer, and in some cases both the originating and receiving unit must confirm. parsed_response.slot_value: Must follow internal police and ministry SOPs for access control, audit logging, and case file preservation, with exception handling allowed for urgent operational situations. Only authorized supervisors or designated officers may approve access to redacted or sensitive records. Temporary access renewal should be approved when the investigation is still active, the officer still has a legitimate need to know, and the original access period is about to expire before the work is complete; it also covers court preparation, follow-up witness checks, and pending forensic review where access is still necessary. Renewal authorization would be by the case supervisor or unit head depending on sensitivity, but the exact approval ladder should be confirmed with the ministry. Any bypass of normal controls should trigger escalation and a mandatory after-the-fact review. If audit logging cannot be fully captured in the moment, a manual incident note and late entry of the reason, approver, and affected records must be completed as soon as possible. In the first release, only a small set of trusted administrators should be able to create, edit, disable, or assign roles to users, and those actions should be logged. Changes in access when someone moves to another station or needs access to a different case should require approval by the local supervisor or records lead rather than happening automatically. Cross-station access should be kept very limited, exposing only what people need for their work. Trusted administrators should be blocked from changing their own critical access, and any action affecting superuser accounts, audit-only accounts, or users in another station should require a second approval or separate admin process. Disabling the last active administrator in a unit should not be allowed without oversight. For exceptional offline approvals, the system should capture the approver’s identity and role, the exact date and time of approval, the user who received the exception, the station or location, the case or incident reference, the specific offline action allowed, the reason for the exception, the expiry or review time if temporary, and whether the approval was made locally or escalated from a higher office.

Only authorized officers and records staff should be able to handle evidence, and every attachment or handoff should log the officer’s identity, date and time, unit, and what was transferred. Updated records should keep the prior version in an audit history; duplicated records should carry a source reference; anything shared with another system should preserve the original retention status. parsed_response.slot_key: Authorization boundaries by role and jurisdiction
parsed_response.slot_value: Authorization should follow the actual police hierarchy and the station or district responsible at that point in the case; when a matter moves between stations or higher authority, the system should show the transfer while keeping a single internal mapping to one standard jurisdiction and authority name despite different local names. When a case needs escalation, it should move to the next supervising officer or the receiving unit, and the case should be reassigned or elevated with the full history preserved. If the receiving unit cannot accept a transferred case immediately, the case should stay in a pending transfer state and the original unit should be notified right away. There should be a time limit for acceptance, and if that passes without action, the case should fall back to the supervising office or return to the sending unit depending on urgency and reason for transfer. The transfer should be stopped or reversed if the case was misrouted, if the receiving unit lacks clearance, or if the transfer would break an active legal or privacy restriction. While the case is in transfer or pending acceptance, the sending unit should be able to view and add notes, but only the current responsible officer or supervisor should be allowed to make the actual update that finalizes the move. The receiving unit should mostly have view-only access until it accepts the case, after which its assigned officer can update the shared record and add new actions. After an escalation, access should usually tighten to the higher-level supervising unit and the new responsible unit, so permissions expand only for the people who need to handle the case and not for everyone in both stations.

parsed_response.slot_value: A simple escalation workflow should be included in the first release so cases do not get stuck. If a case stays in one status too long, the system should flag it and notify the assigned officer and their supervisor first. A supervisor, records lead, or designated admin should be able to trigger escalation manually when there is clear operational need, such as an urgent public safety concern, a stalled investigation, a missing case handoff, or a complaint needing immediate attention from a higher unit. Manual escalation should not be used just to bypass normal routing for convenience, and it should be avoided when the case is under legal restriction, sealed, or already being handled by a special authority unless that authority approves. Any manual override should leave an audit trail with the reason and the person who approved it. In some routine cases the system can also auto-escalate after a set deadline by changing the status to overdue or pending review. Cases involving legal hold, court action, or special investigation should not auto-escalate without supervisor approval. After escalation, the case should be notified and moved to overdue or pending review as applicable, with history preserved.

parsed_response.slot_key: Record update and audit trail expectations
parsed_response.slot_value: Keep the original record when a complaint moves between stations or higher authority, record where it was transferred, when, and to whom so the trail is not lost, and keep an audit trail of every change. Records staff should maintain the official complaint entry, ensure basic details are complete and standardized, correct obvious data issues, manage references, filing numbers, transfers, and the linkage between the complaint and the investigation record, and validate/preserve the proper version when official corrections to names or jurisdiction occur. In practice, the old paper or legacy record is first registered in the new system with a unique reference, the core details are verified (complainant name, date, location, current status), and records staff track what has been transferred while keeping the official master entry. During any short parallel period, updates must be entered into both systems or reconciled by records staff the same day so the versions do not drift apart; after cutover, one clearly designated source of truth must be used and any changes synchronized under that rule. If a case has been transferred or taken over by a higher office, the current controlling office should be the primary jurisdiction shown, but the original station or district name should still be kept in the history. Overrides to reopen a case, change ownership, or edit finalized notes should be allowed only in exceptional situations such as a clerical error, new evidence, a court return, or a supervisory review finding the case was closed too early, and must be approved by a supervisor or higher-ranking officer; in some cases both the originating and receiving unit may need to confirm. Any such override should be logged with the reason, approver, and timestamp so there is a clear audit trail. The initial foundation release should also include audit logging so it is possible to see who viewed or changed what. For manual escalation overrides, the audit trail should additionally capture the user who made the override, the approver if there is one, the exact time, the case number, the status before and after, a short reason or justification, the unit involved, and any comments tied to the decision. The log should be protected so only authorized supervisory or audit users can view it; for sensitive or sealed cases it should be even more restricted, but it must not be deleted or hidden from oversight users.

2. `refuse_current_topic`: Interviewee explicitly refuses to answer or requests to skip the active topic (e.g., "I don't know about this part, let's skip it", "I'd rather not discuss this").
   - target_topic_number: null
3. `switch_existing_topic`: Interviewee explicitly demands to switch to another specific topic present in [topic_catalog] (e.g., "Let's discuss billing first", "Can we jump to user permissions?").
   - target_topic_number: Must be the exact topic_number string (e.g., "topic-1-2") matching the catalog. If no unambiguous match is found, set to null.
4. `return_previous_topic`: Interviewee explicitly requests to navigate back to a previously discussed topic to revise or add details (e.g., "I want to go back and add something to the authentication part").
   - target_topic_number: The target topic_number if specified, otherwise null.
5. `none`: Standard interview response. Interviewee is answering questions, confirming summaries, elaborating on business logic, providing facts, or casually mentioning other modules without requesting a dialog navigation change.
   - target_topic_number: null

# DIMENSION 2: TOPIC VERIFICATION OUTCOME (Active ONLY when Previous Question Strategy == "verify"):
If Previous Question Strategy is NOT "verify":
- `verification_outcome`: "not_applicable"
- `verification_confidence`: 0.0
- `verification_explanation`: null

If Previous Question Strategy is "verify":
- `accepted`: Interviewee explicitly confirms that the active topic's summary is accurate, complete, and needs no revisions or additions (e.g., "Everything looks solid, nothing to add", "The summary covers all our requirements completely, we can move forward", "All requirements captured accurately, no additions needed").

# CONTEXT: A semi-structured interview is underway. You are updating, refining, or extending slots under the target topic based STRICTLY on the interviewee's latest response.
# TASK: Based on the factual information provided by the interviewee in [current_turn_interaction], extract new slot values, refine existing details, identify explicit conflicts, or record deferrals for [current_topic]. If the latest turn contains no new facts or explicit decisions relevant to [current_topic], return an empty array [].

1. Target Topic Description As [current_topic]:
   User roles and responsibilities across investigation, records, and citizen interactions
2. Latest Turn Interaction As [current_turn_interaction]:
   - Interviewer Question: When an authorized supervisor, auditor, or oversight user opens a sensitive or sealed-case escalation log, what practical rules should determine how much detail they can see and whether any part of it must be masked, withheld, or require extra authorization?
   - Interviewee Answer: The practical rule should be least-privilege, so they only see what they need for the specific task they’re doing. If the log includes victim details, informant identities, or protected legal notes, those parts should be masked by default and only revealed with explicit higher authorization or a documented need to know. For sealed cases, the system should show the existence of the action and basic metadata, but withhold the sensitive narrative unless a special clearance or approval is granted.

Extract facts solely from the interviewee's latest response in [current_turn_interaction]. Compare extracted statements against existing slots in [current_topic_slots] and apply these strict operation semantics:

1. "refine" (Compatible Elaboration & Detail Addition):

2. "update" (Initial Population of Empty Slots, Explicit Correction, or Explicit Fact Endorsement):
   - For an empty slot (state="empty"): Populate it with the confirmed fact provided in the latest response. You MUST use operation "update" (NEVER "add") when populating an existing slot from [current_topic_slots], keeping its existing slot_number and slot_key.
   - For a previously uncertain slot (state="uncertain"): If the interviewee now explicitly confirms or finalizes the value, set operation to "update".
   - For an already filled slot (state="filled"):
     * Explicit Correction/Change: When the interviewee explicitly corrects, overrides, or changes the recorded fact with a new decision, use "update" with the newly decided value.
     * Explicit Endorsement of Recorded/Prefilled Fact: When the interviewee explicitly confirms, validates, or endorses an existing/prefilled fact (e.g. agreeing that the recorded goal, audience, or scope is accurate as stated) without altering its substance, use "update" with the confirmed value. This explicitly attaches interview-grounded evidence to the slot.

Do NOT re-emit unchanged old values without direct interviewee endorsement.

3. "add" (Brand-New Distinct Business Attribute Only):
   - Use EXCLUSIVELY when the interviewee introduces a genuinely new requirement attribute that does NOT exist anywhere in [current_topic_slots].
   - Provide a concise business attribute name in slot_key and set slot_number to null.
   - CRITICAL GUARDRAIL: NEVER use "add" for an existing slot in [current_topic_slots], even if its state is "empty"! Populating an existing empty slot is ALWAYS "update". If you specify an existing slot_number with operation "add", the system will reject your output as a contract violation.

   - FORBIDDEN: NEVER overwrite, hijack, or replace an existing slot whose slot_key represents a different business concept! For example, do not overwrite a "Submission Channels" slot with "Operating Hours". Distinct attributes MUST be created via "add" with slot_number=null.

4. "conflict" (Direct Contradiction with Existing Recorded Scope or Decisions):
   - Use when the interviewee's latest statement directly contradicts, negates, or conflicts with a previously recorded fact or scope decision in [current_topic_slots] without explaining why the scope changed.
   - Specific Scope Contradiction: If an existing scope slot states that a capability is OUT OF SCOPE or NOT SUPPORTED for the initial release (e.g. "First version does not support citizen self-submission"), but the interviewee's latest response asserts that it IS supported or included in the first release (e.g. "First version citizens can submit complaints through basic web screen"), you MUST target that existing scope slot, set operation to "conflict", and put the contradictory statement in slot_value. Do NOT silently ignore the conflict or treat it as an independent addition.

5. "mark_uncertain" (Tentative or Provisional Value):
   - Use when the interviewee provides a concrete candidate value but explicitly expresses that it is tentative, subject to confirmation, or might change (e.g., "Tentatively 30 days, awaiting legal review").

6. "defer_uncertain" (Explicit Postponement / Deferral):
   - Use when the interviewee explicitly chooses to defer, postpone, or leave this requirement undecided for now (e.g., "defer for later", "undecided at this moment", "leave tentative").
   - If the slot already has a value, preserve it in slot_value; if empty and no candidate exists, set slot_value to null.

parsed_response.slot_key: Manual escalation audit log access restrictions
parsed_response.slot_value: The audit log should be protected so only authorized supervisory or audit users can view it; for sensitive or sealed cases it should be even more restricted, but it should not be deleted or hidden from oversight users. Only a very small set of users should see sensitive or sealed-case logs, mainly the assigned supervisor, a designated internal auditor, and perhaps a higher-ranking oversight authority if the case is formally sealed or under special review. Supervisors should access it only for legitimate operational reasons, auditors only for compliance or investigation purposes, and both accesses should be logged themselves. If a case is sealed, even those users should see only the minimum necessary detail, with the most sensitive content masked unless there is explicit authorization. When an authorized supervisor, auditor, or oversight user opens a sensitive or sealed-case escalation log, they should follow least-privilege access so they only see what is needed for the specific task; victim details, informant identities, and protected legal notes should be masked by default and revealed only with explicit higher authorization or a documented need to know. For sealed cases, the system should show the existence of the action and basic metadata, but withhold the sensitive narrative unless special clearance or approval is granted.
